source_notes: OpenCover distinguishes colloquial DeFi insurance language from onchain cover or onchain risk transfer.
NAIC describes parametric insurance as generally regulated under traditional insurance frameworks where specific parametric rules are absent.
NAIC McCarran-Ferguson material emphasizes U.S. state primacy in insurance regulation.
FinCEN 2019 CVC guidance distinguishes hosted wallets where a host has independent control from unhosted wallets where users control funds.

bekemeier_defi_insurability_2023.relevance: Academic taxonomy of DeFi risk transfer and smart-contract risk insurability; identifies actuarial, oracle, governance, and regulatory-compliance challenges.

nadler_bekemeier_schar_defi_risk_transfe.relevance: Academic DeFi risk-transfer protocol design; useful as a technical comparison, not a legal clearance source.

zhou_zhang_defi_insurance_conundrums_202.relevance: Journal article identifying liquidity, actuarial, verification, scale, yield, exploitation, cybersecurity, and regulation conundrums in DeFi insurance.

mik_oracle_problem_insurtech_2023.relevance: Legal/InsurTech analysis of smart contracts, oracle dependence, trigger definition, and parametric payout automation.

iais_fintech_developments_insurance_2022.relevance: Insurance-supervisor report noting DeFi protection coverages and uncertainty over insurance classification and regulatory approach.

eiopa_blockchain_smart_contracts_insuran.relevance: Insurance-supervisor feedback on blockchain and smart contracts; emphasizes use-case specificity, consumer protection, existing regulatory frameworks, and regulatory sandboxes.

naic_parametric_disaster_insurance.relevance: U.S. insurance-regulator material treating parametric disaster products as insurance policies generally under traditional insurance frameworks where specific rules are absent.

naic_mccarran_ferguson_state_regulation.relevance: U.S. state-based insurance regulation background; supports jurisdiction-by-jurisdiction counsel review.

fincen_cvc_guidance_2019.relevance: CVC guidance distinguishing hosted and unhosted wallet control and DApp money-transmission risk when accepting and transmitting value.

opencover_onchain_cover_language.relevance: Industry wording example distinguishing regulated insurance terminology from onchain cover or onchain risk transfer.

decision: No ZenoCover user sale, launch, premium collection, policy issuance, insurance-language marketing, public underwriting claim, custody, value transmission, broker/intermediary role, cover-term recommendation, user-specific recommendation, claim-adjustment discretion, guaranteed payout, pooled risk-bearing, or operator-run pool is allowed from current artifacts.
